Facility Inventory & Condition Assessmen.justification: Comprehensive district-wide inventory including detailed data on building age, size, classrooms, specialized spaces, and site plans. Robust condition assessments cover major systems (HVAC, plumbing, roofs, electrical, lighting, technology, accessibility) with detailed scoring and connection to student outcomes and long-term capital planning (e.g., pages 13-150).

Enrollment & Capacity Planning.justification: Includes detailed enrollment projections with methodology, demographic trends, and housing data. Capacity utilization is analyzed by site and grade with explicit strategies for addressing under- and over-capacity, including school reconstruction, modernization, and adaptive reuse (e.g., demographic study pages 281-291, master plan proposals).

Educational Alignment.justification: Educational goals and mission are integrated as core organizing principles. Facility projects are directly linked to educational needs including flexible multi-use spaces, STEM, special education, and technology-rich environments. Plans include detailed educational specifications and programmatic considerations (e.g., master plan proposals pages 157-210).

Outdoor Spaces & Greening.justification: Plan provides data and analysis of outdoor spaces including play areas, ball fields, and site furnishings. Strategies for improvements such as artificial turf, irrigation upgrades, and exterior lunch canopies are included, but districtwide greening data and climate resilience framing are limited (e.g., site assessments and master plan proposals).

Climate Risk & Mitigation.justification: Acknowledges climate-related issues such as water conservation and energy efficiency. Includes some strategies like shade structures and irrigation system upgrades, but lacks comprehensive climate risk assessment or districtwide climate resilience as a central theme (e.g., master plan proposals on energy efficiency and water conservation).

Energy Efficiency & Resilience.justification: Includes energy efficiency strategies such as LED lighting upgrades, HVAC replacements, and solar panel installations. References state requirements (Title 24, ZNE goals) and energy resilience goals, but lacks fully comprehensive districtwide energy resilience and electrification plans (e.g., master plan proposals pages 157-210).

Financial Plan & Capital Strategy.justification: Presents detailed, itemized cost estimates for all projects with prioritization by safety, building integrity, and future needs. Includes multiple funding sources such as bonds, state grants, developer fees, and alternative financing. Demonstrates alignment of financial capacity with educational and facility priorities (e.g., project budget estimates pages 219-273, funding resources pages 275-278).
